title: Metric Explorer: Heatmap & Multi-series View for Model/Route Performance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Design a compact, scannable 'Metric Explorer' panel within Redwood Console that surfaces per-model and per-route performance across latency, throughput, and token-level metrics. The explorer should let engineers and product owners quickly identify regressions or hotspots, compare model variants, and dive into time ranges with minimal clicks. This ticket focuses on the UX patterns and chart specifications — heatmap overview + multi-series time chart + token distribution histogram + exportable CSV — and a high-fidelity prototype for designer/engineer handoff.
background: Current per-route dashboards are list-heavy and require multiple page loads to compare models. Customers request a single-pane exploratory workflow: overview for anomaly detection, lightweight comparison between two routes or model revisions, and pre-baked chart exports for postmortems. Instrumentation endpoints are being shipped by ENG-3078 (metric tags) and ENG-3120 (rollup store).
requirements: Overview heatmap showing 24h latency percentiles by route/model (configurable percentile buckets)
Multi-series time chart for P50/P95/P99 latency and tokens/sec, with synchronized brushing to change time range
Token distribution histogram (per-request token counts) with median/90th markers
Quick-compare modal: choose up to 3 models or routes and show delta lines with percentage change badges
Export button for CSV and PNG of current view
Lightweight annotation support to pin notes (e.g., deploys, infra incidents)
Mobile/responsive considerations: collapse heatmap to affordance icon on small widths
Accessibility: keyboard navigation for series toggles and ARIA labels for chart regions
chart_specifications: Heatmap overview: X axis = rolling 24h in 15-minute buckets, Y axis = route/model rows, cell color = P95 latency (ms) with diverging scale: green <= 200ms, yellow 200-500ms, red > 500ms; tooltip: route, model, bucket start, P50/P95/P99, requests

Multi-series time chart: stacked lines for P50 (solid), P95 (dashed), P99 (dot-dash); secondary axis for tokens/sec; colors follow brand palette (blue, purple, orange); hover crosshair shows exact values and request sample count; legend supports toggle and mute
Token distribution: histogram with 10 bins by default, log scale toggle, overlay vertical lines for median and 90th percentile; histogram supports brushing to filter time series
Delta comparison: show percent delta next to series label with color-coded chip (green negative latency = good, red positive latency = regression); baseline selection persists across routes
Sampling: charts default to aggregated rollups (1-minute) and fall back to sampled raw events when querying >30d; UX should expose sample rate badge
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma screens for desktop and tablet completed and reviewed by PM and ENG
Chart specs handed off as JSON-style chart spec list and validated against ENG instrumentation (ENG-3078, ENG-3120)
Prototype demonstrates heatmap -> chart drill flow and compare modal, including keyboard navigation
Design review notes addressed and updated assets uploaded to Drive
Handoff ticket created for ENG work with annotated assets and edge-case list
risks_and_open_questions: Rollup latency buckets: confirm with ENG whether P95 computation across rollups can be done on the server or requires client-side combining
How much cardinality on routes/models can the heatmap support before we need virtualized rows? (performance & UX trade-off)
Chart library choice: we prefer a shared Redwood chart component but need to validate multi-axis and heatmap support
Annotation model: will annotations be global (console-wide) or scoped per-tenant route? Affects permissions and storage
